description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake loaded with an abundance of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions, all bound in a perfectly crisp, golden batter. It offers a delightful contrast of chewy seafood and tender vegetables with a satisfyingly crunchy exterior, making it a popular street food and appetizer. Serve it hot with a tangy soy-based dipping sauce for an unforgettable culinary experience.

ingredients.notes: cleaned and chopped into bite-sized pieces
Soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, sesame seeds

instructions.title: Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Clean and prepare your mixed seafood, chopping larger pieces into bite-sized chunks. Pat them dry thoroughly to prevent a watery batter. Wash and trim the green onions, cutting them into 3-4 inch lengths. Thinly slice the half onion and red chili if using.

instructions.title: Make the Pancake Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, cold water, eggs, 2 tablespoons of soy sauce, and salt until a smooth batter forms. Be careful not to overmix; a few small lumps are acceptable. The batter should be slightly thick, similar to a crepe batter.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients
instructions.text: Add the prepared seafood and sliced onion to the batter. Gently fold them in until evenly distributed. Do not add the green onions to the batter yet, as they will be placed directly in the pan.

instructions.title: Heat the Pan and Add Batter
instructions.text: Heat a large, non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, ensuring it coats the bottom evenly. Pour about 1/3 to 1/2 of the batter mixture into the hot pan, spreading it out to form a thin, round pancake.

instructions.title: Arrange Green Onions and Cook
instructions.text: Quickly arrange a generous layer of green onion pieces on top of the wet batter in a single direction. You can also add a few slices of red chili for color and a hint of spice. Cook for 3-5 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy.

instructions.title: Flip and Cook Second Side
instructions.text: Carefully flip the pancake using a large spatula. Add a little more oil around the edges if needed. Press down gently to ensure even cooking. Cook for another 3-5 minutes until the second side is golden brown and crispy, and the seafood is cooked through.

instructions.title: Serve with Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: Slide the cooked Haemul Pajeon onto a cutting board. Repeat with the remaining batter. Cut the pancake into wedges or squares. Serve immediately with a simple dipping sauce made from soy sauce, a splash of vinegar, a drizzle of sesame oil, and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

tips: Use cold water for the batter to help create a crispier pancake. Some chefs even use sparkling water for an extra airy texture.
For the best flavor, use a variety of fresh seafood. If fresh is unavailable, good quality frozen mixed seafood can be used, just ensure it is fully thawed and thoroughly patted dry.
Serve Haemul Pajeon immediately after cooking to enjoy its optimal crispy texture. It pairs wonderfully with a simple soy-based dipping sauce and a cold Korean beverage.
article:
Sizzling, savory, and bursting with the fresh flavors of the sea, Haemul Pajeon is more than just a pancake – it's a culinary experience that transports you straight to the bustling streets of Seoul. This beloved Korean seafood pancake is a staple in homes and restaurants alike, cherished for its crispy edges, tender interior, and generous medley of seafood and vibrant green onions. Whether you're a seasoned Korean food enthusiast or a curious newcomer, mastering the art of Haemul Pajeon is a rewarding journey that promises delicious results. Get ready to dive into the world of this iconic dish, from its essential ingredients to pro tips for achieving that perfect golden crisp.

## What is Haemul Pajeon (Korean Seafood Pancake)?

Haemul Pajeon translates literally to "seafood scallion pancake," with "Haemul" meaning seafood and "Pajeon" referring to a scallion pancake. Unlike the sweet, fluffy pancakes you might enjoy for breakfast, Haemul Pajeon is a distinctly savory dish, often served as an appetizer, a side dish, or a light meal. Its charm lies in the harmonious contrast of textures and flavors: the crispiness of the pan-fried batter, the slight chewiness of the seafood, and the fresh bite of the green onions, all complemented by a tangy dipping sauce.

Historically, pancakes like pajeon have been a part of Korean cuisine for centuries, evolving from simple vegetable fritters to more elaborate versions incorporating meat and seafood. Haemul Pajeon gained particular popularity for its ability to showcase the abundant seafood available along Korea's coasts. It's a dish often enjoyed during rainy days, paired with a bowl of makgeolli (Korean rice wine), creating a cozy and comforting atmosphere. The key to an outstanding Haemul Pajeon is a perfectly balanced batter – light enough to allow the ingredients to shine, yet robust enough to achieve a satisfying crispness.

## Ingredients You Need for Haemul Pajeon

Creating an authentic Haemul Pajeon starts with sourcing fresh, quality ingredients. While the exact proportions can be adjusted to your taste, here’s a comprehensive list of what you’ll need to whip up this delightful Korean seafood pancake:

For the Batter:
*   1 cup all-purpose flour (or a mix of all-purpose and glutinous rice flour for extra chewiness)
*   1/2 cup potato starch or cornstarch (for crispiness)
*   1 1/2 cups cold water or anchovy broth (broth adds depth of flavor)
*   1 large egg
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   Pinch of black pepper

For the Filling:
*   2 cups green onions (scallions), cut into 2-3 inch lengths (white and light green parts preferred)
*   1/2 lb mixed seafood, such as shrimp (peeled, deveined, and cut into bite-sized pieces), squid (cleaned and thinly sliced), and mussels or clams (shelled)
*   1/2 small onion, thinly sliced (optional)
*   1/4 cup sliced red bell pepper (optional, for color and sweetness)
*   2-3 green chili peppers, thinly sliced (optional, for a spicy kick)

For Cooking:
*   Vegetable oil or any neutral cooking oil (plenty for frying)

For the Dipping Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon rice vinegar
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
*   1/2 teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, optional)
*   1 clove garlic, minced (optional)

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Haemul Pajeon

Follow these simple steps to create a mouth-watering Haemul Pajeon that will impress your family and friends:

1.  **Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables:** Thoroughly clean and pat dry all your seafood. Cut shrimp into bite-sized pieces if large, and slice squid into rings or strips. Prepare the green onions by washing them and cutting them into 2-3 inch segments. Thinly slice the optional onion, bell pepper, and chili peppers.

2.  **Make the Batter:** In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, potato starch (or cornstarch), salt, and black pepper. Gradually add the cold water (or broth) and the egg, whisking continuously until a smooth batter forms. The consistency should be similar to a thin pancake batter – not too thick, not too watery. Avoid overmixing, as this can make the pancake tough.

3.  **Combine Ingredients (Optional, for easier handling):** While some prefer to add ingredients directly to the pan, for easier handling and even distribution, you can gently fold about half of the prepared green onions, seafood, and other optional vegetables into the batter. Reserve the other half for arranging on top in the pan.

4.  **Heat the Pan:** Place a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add a generous amount of cooking oil, enough to coat the bottom of the pan thickly (about 2-3 tablespoons). Let the oil heat up until it shimmers slightly.

5.  **Cook the Pancake:** Pour about 1 to 1.5 cups of the batter mixture into the hot pan, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake about 8-10 inches in diameter. If you reserved some ingredients, quickly arrange the remaining green onions and seafood artfully on top of the wet batter.

6.  **Flip and Cook Until Golden:** Cook for 4-5 minutes on the first side, or until the edges turn golden brown and crispy, and the bottom is set. You can gently lift an edge with a spatula to check. Once ready, carefully flip the Haemul Pajeon using a wide spatula. Add another splash of oil around the edges if needed to ensure crispiness. Cook for another 3-4 minutes on the second side until it's also golden brown and cooked through. Press down lightly with your spatula to ensure good contact with the pan and encourage crispiness.

7.  **Serve Immediately:** Carefully slide the cooked Haemul Pajeon onto a cutting board. Cut it into wedges or squares using a pizza cutter or knife. Serve piping hot with the prepared dipping sauce on the side.

## Pro Tips for the Best Haemul Pajeon

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Haemul Pajeon requires a few insider tricks. Here’s how to elevate your homemade seafood pancake:

*   **Cold Batter is Key:** Using very cold water (or even sparkling water for extra lightness) for your batter helps create a crispier texture. The temperature difference between the cold batter and hot oil creates steam, resulting in a lighter, airier pancake.
*   **Don't Skimp on Oil:** Haemul Pajeon is not meant to be cooked with minimal oil. A generous amount of oil is crucial for achieving those coveted crispy, golden-brown edges. Think shallow-frying rather than light pan-frying.
*   **High Heat, Then Medium:** Start with a medium-high heat to get the pan and oil hot, which will quickly crisp the exterior. Once the batter is poured, you can reduce the heat slightly to medium to ensure the inside cooks through without burning the outside.
*   **Thin Batter, Crispy Outcome:** A slightly thinner batter allows for more surface area to crisp up. If your batter seems too thick, add a tablespoon or two of cold water until it reaches the desired consistency.
*   **Fresh Seafood Matters:** The fresher your seafood, the better your Haemul Pajeon will taste. Avoid overcooking the seafood, as it can become rubbery.
*   **Press Down Gently:** After flipping, gently press down on the pancake with your spatula. This helps ensure even cooking and maximizes contact with the hot pan, leading to a more consistent crispiness.

## Serving Suggestions for Haemul Pajeon

Haemul Pajeon is a versatile dish that can be enjoyed in various ways. Traditionally, it's served as an appetizer or a communal dish.

*   **The Essential Dipping Sauce:** A simple yet flavorful dipping sauce is non-negotiable. The recipe provided earlier (soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, sesame seeds, gochugaru, minced garlic) is a classic. The tanginess and subtle heat perfectly cut through the richness of the pancake.
*   **Makgeolli Pairing:** For an authentic Korean experience, pair your Haemul Pajeon with a chilled bottle of makgeolli. The slightly sweet, fizzy rice wine is the quintessential companion, especially on a rainy day.
*   **Korean Side Dishes (Banchan):** Serve it alongside an array of banchan like kimchi, pickled radishes, or seasoned spinach for a complete meal experience.
*   **As a Light Meal:** While often an appetizer, a large Haemul Pajeon can easily serve as a satisfying light lunch or dinner, especially when accompanied by rice or a simple salad.

## Variations and Substitutions for Your Seafood Pancake

While the classic Haemul Pajeon is a beloved standard, don't hesitate to experiment with variations to suit your taste or what you have on hand.

*   **Vegetarian Pajeon:** For a meat-free option, omit the seafood entirely. You can make a delicious Kimchi Pajeon by adding chopped kimchi and its juice to the batter, or a simple Vegetable Pajeon with mushrooms, carrots, zucchini, and bell peppers.
*   **Different Seafood:** Feel free to customize your seafood mix. Oysters, small octopus pieces, or even crab meat can be fantastic additions. Just ensure all seafood is cut to a similar size for even cooking.
*   **Spice It Up:** If you love heat, increase the amount of green chili peppers or add a spoonful of gochujang (Korean chili paste) to the batter for a deeper, spicier flavor profile.
*   **Herbs and Aromatics:** Experiment with adding other fresh herbs like chives or a dash of finely grated ginger to the batter for an extra layer of aroma.

With these tips and instructions, you're well on your way to creating a delicious and authentic Haemul Pajeon in your own kitchen. This savory seafood pancake is more than just food; it's a celebration of Korean culinary tradition, offering a delightful combination of textures and flavors that will leave you craving more. So grab your ingredients, fire up the pan, and get ready to enjoy a taste of Korea!
